ImageDescription.value:
A freshwater ostracod of genus Heterocypris (Heterocypris sp.) photographed under a microscope using an 8x objective. The specimen was collected from a pond in Rakvere, Estonia, in April 2024. The image clearly shows the characteristic bivalved carapace of the ostracod, which is semi-transparent with a greenish-yellow coloration. The fine setae along the edge of the carapace and the characteristic antennae are particularly well visible. The antennae extending from the carapace are important locomotory organs for ostracods.

The specimen was photographed against a black background, which excellently highlights the semi-transparent structure of the animal's carapace and its delicate appendages. The lighting technique used differs from conventional transmitted microscope illumination - instead, reflected light from a photographic speedlight flash was used. This lighting solution allows for exceptional detail in revealing the object's surface texture and transparent structures.

The image was created using focus stacking technique, which allows achieving great depth of field even in microscopic photography. This technique is particularly important when photographing microorganisms, as it enables sharp details to be captured in both the near and far portions of the subject.

Categories.value: Hydrachnidia|Self-published work|Focus stacking images of Arachnida|Featured pictures of animals in Estonia|Teadusfoto pildikorje 2024|Uploaded via Campaign:Teadus|Featured pictures by Janek Lass

ImageDescription.value:
A water mite (Hydrachnidia) photographed in lateral view under a microscope using an 8x objective. The specimen was collected in May 2023. Water mites represent one of the most diverse and abundant groups of aquatic invertebrates. The lateral view particularly emphasizes the characteristic spherical body of water mites, with its translucent surface displaying a beautiful bluish-green iridescence. The limbs with their distinctive spiny bristles are also clearly visible.
The specimen was photographed against a black background, which excellently highlights the texture of the semi-transparent body surface and the fine details of the appendages. The lighting technique used was reflected light from a photographic speedlight flash, which particularly emphasizes the surface structures and metallic sheen of the carapace. The image was created using focus stacking technique, which ensures great depth of field throughout the subject.

Categories.value: Heterocypris incongruens|Images with annotations|Self-published work|Featured pictures of animals in Estonia|Focus stacking images of Crustacea|Teadusfoto pildikorje 2024|Uploaded via Campaign:Teadus|Featured pictures by Janek Lass

ImageDescription.value: A freshwater ostracod (Heterocypris incongruens) photographed under a microscope using an 8x objective lens. The specimen was collected from an urban pond in May 2024. The image prominently features the characteristic muscle scar pattern located on the inner surface of the carapace. This pattern consists of clusters of oval marks that represent the attachment points of muscles used to open and close the shell. This trait is species-specific and critical for accurate identification. Additionally, the semi-transparent greenish-yellow carapace is visible, along with fine setae along the edge, which assist the ostracod in locomotion and anchoring in its environment. The image was captured using reflected light, which highlights the surface texture of the carapace and the muscle scar impressions. A focus stacking technique was employed, ensuring excellent depth of field and sharp detail throughout the entire subject.
